dialogue.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me what happened and how your right hip and leg are feeling right now?

I was in a car accident - someone hit me from behind while I was stopped. My right groin area is killing me, it's really severe pain, and both my knees hurt too. My right leg just feels... wrong, like I can't position it normally.
Can you describe how your right leg looks right now — is it shortened, rotated inward or outward, and can you move it at all?
Yes, my right leg looks shorter than my left one, and it's kind of bent and turned inward. I can barely move it at all - any attempt to move it makes the groin pain so much worse.

This sounds like a posterior hip dislocation. Given the mechanism—dashboard-type injury in a collision with knee trauma—I'd like to check your knees too: do you have pain, swelling, or deformity there, or any numbness/tingling down the leg?

Yes, both my knees are painful, especially when I try to bend them, but I don't think they're swollen or look deformed. I don't have any numbness or tingling down my leg though, just that terrible pain in my groin.
Any numbness or weakness in your foot, or can you still move your toes and feel your foot normally?
I can move my toes and feel my foot okay - no numbness or weakness there. It's really just the groin pain and not being able to move my hip that's the problem.
I'd like to get imaging to confirm — REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_and_Hip_X-Ray
RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray shows no fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.
Given the dashboard mechanism, I also want to check your knees for any occult injury — REQUEST TEST: Knee_X-Ray_Bilateral

RESULTS: Knee X-rays are not available in the provided data.

NORMAL READINGS - No fractures or dislocations identified in bilateral knee imaging. Patellofemoral joints appear intact with normal alignment.
